scope: The standing and partial post-restoration Halidzor fortress above Kapan: the irregular basalt enclosure and round tower, southern entrance and stairs, the fortified church and its wings, the north tomb and low monastic traces, and the nearby eastern single-nave village church ruins.

primaryWrittenSources.section: Armenian state register, Syunik, Bekh, monument group 8.1 and adjacent village site 8.2
primaryWrittenSources.facts: The seventeenth-century church was refortified in 1723. Two-story residential wings adjoin its north and south. A four-pier domed tomb and a refectory stand to the north. The separately listed village church to the east is single-nave.

primaryWrittenSources.section: Armenian Academy architecture survey, Halidzor section ending near p. 606
primaryWrittenSources.facts: Its irregular quadrilateral follows a steep Voghji slope. The church has massive rough basalt walls and narrow openings, with defended upper floors in the attached ranges. Wall thickness is about one metre. A circular tower occupies the vulnerable southwest corner.
The present visible entrance is in the south wall and the southwestern round tower survives. Further round tower remains exist within the complex.
The regional heritage service reported the 2006–2010 repairs and steps linking the entrance and church, around 20 metres apart. Open gateway and ruin gaps were still present at the time.
